questions.question: Debris and oil often collect in which part of a traffic lane?

options.text: Where motorcycle riders should always travel
Where drivers are least likely to see a motorcycle

questions.explanation: Debris and oil collect in the center of the lane. Other hazards like utility hole covers are also found there.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it signals a hazard on the right side of the road. Signals help riders communicate when riding in groups.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding to the side risks a collision. Riding too far away may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Stay flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: When it is raining, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane
Off to the side of the road until it stops
In the tire tracks left by cars

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is slippery, especially when rain first starts. Oil from cars hasn't washed away yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the best choice.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, which of these does NOT need adjustment?
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how the motorcycle sits. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in crashes had been drinking.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a major cause of motorcycle crashes and deaths. Studies show that 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle accidents had been drinking.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: Will stay the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle

questions.explanation: Extra weight increases the motorcycle's inertia and stopping distance. Start slowing and stopping earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes
questions.explanation: In risky areas like school zones or construction, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces your reaction time if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag
Pack lighter items near the front
Avoid placing items over the rear axle
Place items behind the rear axle

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting weight behind the rear axle can affect control.

questions.question: If road conditions require a longer stopping distance than normal, what should you do?

options.text: Ask someone else to operate your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: You need more following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This applies when the road is slippery, when you cannot see past the vehicle in front of you, or when traffic is heavy. Keep at least a three-second distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction opposite of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the same side as your turn. Press the opposite handgrip to turn back to your original direction after you are clear of the hazard.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, where should you position yourself?

options.text: On the right side of the lane so they can see you in their side mirror.
On the left side of the lane so you can see better ahead.
In the center of the lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to draw attention to yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane so you can see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to see better ahead and be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: When must you report a traffic crash to the police?

options.text: When the crash involves two or more vehicles.
When the crash involves an animal, such as a deer.
When the crash results in damage of at least $1,000.
When the crash happens on a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the crash results in damage of at least $1,000.
questions.explanation: You must report a crash to local police, the sheriff, or the State Highway Patrol if it causes at least $1,000 in damage, or if anyone is injured or killed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: What is the proper footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels may catch on rough surfaces. Keep laces tucked in so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: What type of sign can be rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular and white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars in traffic?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs the same stopping distance as a car in traffic.

questions.question: When must a motorcycle passenger wear a helmet?

options.text: If they are under 18 years old.
If the operator's license is two years old or newer.

questions.correctAnswerText: If they are under 18 years old.
questions.explanation: Any passenger under 18 must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards. If the operator must wear a helmet, the passenger must also wear one, no matter their age. All riders should wear helmets on every ride.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes hard while leaning.

questions.explanation: Straighten and square the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten your motorcycle, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle, then increase braking pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from the wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield stops your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind. A windshield does not provide this protection. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing can guarantee that a driver sees you. The safest approach is to assume that if another vehicle could enter your path, it will.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when either brake lever is used.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter to apply the brake when downshifting.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when either brake lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either the front or rear brake lever, both brakes apply. Read your motorcycle's owner's manual to learn more about your specific braking system.

questions.question: How should you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push on the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, push the left handgrip, then push the right to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.
